<issue>Issue Title: [Bug] Parallel invocations to the same Agent instance corrupt message history
Description:
### Problem Statement
Currently, if an invocation occurs while another one is being processed, the internal global state of the agent becomes corrupted, causing not only the concurrent invocations to fail, but also any subsequent invocations to fail.
A common scenario affected by this behavior is when a retry occurs due to client timeout, which triggers another invocation with the same session ID while the previous request is still being processed.
### Proposed Solution
Throw a concurrency exception instead of handling the request and corrupting the agent's state, which causes all subsequent calls to fail.
### Use Case
This is most impactful retries retries, but also a general protection for the agent's state.

This snippet shows the definition of the "Agent" class in the "src/strands/agent/agent.py" file. The class constructor (__init__) initializes various parameters including model, messages, tools, prompts, state, session_manager, and others. There are several properties and methods including __call__, which appears to be the method for invoking the agent with a prompt and additional arguments. The class seems to be the core agent implementation managing its state and processing requests.

2. What is the relationship between this part of the code and the bug?

The bug describes corruption of the agent's internal state during concurrent invocations. Since this "Agent" class encapsulates the state (such as messages, session_manager, and state), it is directly related to the bug. In particular, concurrent calls to the Agent instance's __call__ method or other methods that mutate the state could lead to concurrency issues. Understanding this class and especially the methods used during invocation is crucial to fixing the bug.

3. Given the issue description, what would be the intended behavior of this part of the code?

The intended behavior is that when multiple concurrent invocations to the same Agent instance occur, some concurrency control should prevent the internal state from being corrupted. Instead of allowing parallel execution that mutates shared mutable state, the code should throw a concurrency exception if an invocation is in progress, thus protecting the agent's internal global state and ensuring subsequent calls are successful.
